content.text: Spring is a lightweight framework designed for developing enterprise Java applications, but developers often face several challenges when using it:

items: Spring applications require numerous configurations, often in XML files.
Different environments (e.g., production, development, testing) may require different configurations, such as varying database connections.
Example: A testing team may need a separate database from the development team, which adds complexity and increases configuration time.
Developers must manually search for compatible dependencies for their specific Spring version and configure them.
Selecting incorrect versions of dependencies can cause issues that are difficult to resolve.
For every new feature, the appropriate dependency must be identified and integrated.
Servers (e.g., Tomcat, Jetty) must be explicitly configured to run Spring applications.

Spring does not provide automatic protection against security threats like XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) or CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery), requiring developers to implement security measures manually.
Developers need to write a significant amount of boilerplate code to perform even basic tasks.
Spring offers various ways to achieve the same task, which can confuse developers, and selecting the wrong option can lead to project failure.

content.text: Spring Boot is designed to address the challenges of Spring development by simplifying the process and increasing productivity.

items: Spring Boot is an add-on to the Spring Framework, designed to make Spring-based application development quicker and easier.
It reduces the need for boilerplate code and configuration, allowing developers to focus more on business logic.
Eliminates Boilerplate Configuration: Spring Boot minimizes XML and configuration code.
Embedded Servers: Provides embedded servers (e.g., Tomcat, Jetty) so developers don't need to set up a separate server.
Starter Dependencies: Spring Boot comes with pre-configured starter dependencies that automatically configure libraries and services required for the application.
Production-Ready Features: Provides features like health checks, metrics, and application monitoring.
No XML Configuration: Configuration is handled via Java classes and properties files, reducing complexity.
Opinionated Framework: Spring Boot comes with sensible defaults, allowing developers to start quickly without needing extensive configuration.
Customization: Despite having defaults, Spring Boot allows developers to override and customize settings based on project needs.
Auto-Configuration: Spring Boot configures applications automatically based on the classpath, eliminating the need for manual configuration.

content.text: Starters in Spring Boot simplify the process of adding libraries to your application. These are pre-configured dependencies for commonly used libraries.

items: spring-boot-starter-web: For building web applications using Spring MVC and Spring REST with an embedded Tomcat server.
spring-boot-starter-data-jpa: For integrating Spring Data JPA with Hibernate.
spring-boot-starter-test: Provides support for testing with libraries like JUnit and Mockito.
spring-boot-starter-actuator: Adds support for Spring Boot Actuator, which provides production-ready features like health checks and metrics.
spring-boot-starter-log4j2: Replaces the default logging with Log4j2.

content.text: Spring Boot uses auto-configuration to set up the application based on the dependencies available in the classpath. This means developers don't need to manually configure everything.

items: If JDBC dependencies are present in the classpath, Spring Boot will automatically configure the database connection without needing explicit configuration in XML files.

content.text: Spring Boot provides two main interfaces for performing actions after the application has started.
The CommandLineRunner interface provides a run() method that is executed after the application context is loaded.
Similar to CommandLineRunner, ApplicationRunner provides a run() method but with the difference that it accepts ApplicationArguments instead of a string array.

items: FailureAnalyzer: Provides error messages with actions to fix failures when the application fails to start.
Lazy Initialization: Beans are created only when needed, rather than during startup.
Database Support: Spring Boot supports SQL databases and NoSQL technologies like MongoDB and Neo4J.
Availability States: Spring Boot supports Liveliness (whether the application can recover from failures) and Readiness (whether the application can handle traffic) states.

content.text: Spring Boot simplifies Spring application development by eliminating the need for complex configurations, reducing boilerplate code, and offering built-in features like embedded servers and auto-configuration. By streamlining the development process, it increases productivity and reduces the development time.
